q: The Picard-Lindelöf theorem guarantees unique local solutions to ẋ = f(x,t), x(t₀) = x₀ when f is:
opts: Locally Lipschitz in x and continuous in t
exp: Picard-Lindelöf: local Lipschitz in x + continuity in t → unique local solution. The proof uses the Banach contraction on the space of continuous functions. The condition is sharp: without Lipschitz (e.g., f = |x|^{1/2}), uniqueness fails.
